description: M6/M7 vs. the alternative (docs/vision/27-strengths-bench.md §6, plan docs/plans/strengths-bench.md SB-32): the home lookup corpus (testdata/contextbench/tasks-home.json, ids kept, prompts and ground truth copied verbatim) run as scenariobench tasks with five arms — full (fathom, wired), graphify, serena, gopls (each a competitor's own MCP tool documented in docs/bench/competitors.md), and grep (no MCP at all). Every arm gets Read/Grep/Bash; only 'full' is wired and gets the fathom stanza ('stanza'); every other arm's instructions variant is 'plain' — the subject's own files, untouched. This corpus's tasks are LOOKUPS, not code changes, so Oracle (fail_to_pass/pass_to_pass/coverage) is deliberately left empty for every task: the graded answer is a short string, not a test result. The expected ground truth for each task lives in notes.gold (SB-32's instruction: 'put gold under notes'), keyed by task id, copied from tasks-home.json's own ground_truth/scoring_rule/class fields — see notes.gold_source for the exact pointer instead of duplicating tasks-home.json's multi-paragraph provenance essays here. A FRESHNESS task (id FRESH-M7-01, category 'freshness', M7) is added: its Subject.PostWireSetup writes a brand-new file and function AFTER the arm's own setup AND the wired arm's first ingest have already run (O45 item 4) — see notes.freshness_run_order for the ordering this task depends on. Task categories for the 13 lookup tasks are hand-assigned from tasks-home.json's own class taxonomy (obligations, verify, blast_radius, claim_provenance, concern_search, contradiction, staleness) per types.go's 'Category ... assigned by ... hand with a derivation note' allowance — none of them are a ClassifyChange shape, because none of them is a code change.

full.prediction: Wins the obligations/verify/staleness lookups outright (no competitor tool answers governance questions at all); wins or ties the two structural lookups (2-hop callers, interface implementers) via find_callers/blast_radius and find_symbol's implementations field; wins the freshness task because the wired worktree is (re-)ingested after the scripted edit lands; ties everyone on the pure-prose contradiction task, where no index has an edge.

graphify.prediction: Its query_graph/get_neighbors/shortest_path tools answer code structure, not documented governance rules, so it is predicted to tie the grep arm (not fathom) on every obligations/verify/staleness lookup; a plausible tie with fathom on the 2-hop caller lookup (a direct calls-relation edge, its home turf); a predicted loss on the interface-implementers lookup (no type-checker, so implicit Go interface satisfaction is outside what tree-sitter extraction can encode); a predicted loss on the freshness task (its graph.json is a precomputed artifact built during this arm's own setup, before the freshness edit lands, and this arm's setup runs no --update afterward).
graphify.notes: setup is the headless CLI build (graphify update <path> --no-cluster: tree-sitter only, no LLM, no plugin install) — `graphify install` writes a Claude Code skill into the user's global config and `/graphify .` is an in-session slash command, neither of which a bench may run (docs/bench/competitors.md)
graphify.instructions_text:
## graphify code navigation

Graphify's own MCP tools are this repository's way to answer where a
symbol is defined, who calls it, and what breaks if it changes —
`query_graph`, `get_node`, `get_neighbors`, and `shortest_path`,
backed by a precomputed graph.json. Read files to *edit* them, not
to discover them.

Reach for these first where they apply (who calls it, what breaks); elsewhere the nearest structural query is still worth trying before grep.

Opening moves by task shape (first 1-2 calls, then edit):
- obligations: query_graph for the symbol's neighbourhood, then grep the nearest CLAUDE.md / ADR.md
- claim_provenance: get_node for the symbol's own record, then grep ADR.md for the citation
- concern_search: query_graph for a pattern over node labels, then grep the doc comment text
- contradiction: query_graph for a pattern over node labels, then grep both documents directly
- freshness: graph_stats for the artifact's own build metadata, then grep the file on disk
- staleness: graph_stats for the artifact's own build metadata, then grep the cited file
- verify: query_graph for the symbol's presence, then grep the plan/gate text directly
- blast_radius: get_neighbors -> shortest_path, edges chained twice

serena.prediction: find_symbol/find_referencing_symbols/find_implementations answer code structure, not documented governance rules, so it is predicted to tie the grep arm (not fathom) on every obligations/verify/staleness lookup; a plausible tie with fathom on the 2-hop caller lookup (find_referencing_symbols chained twice) and the interface-implementers lookup (find_implementations is backed by gopls's real type-checker — single-language references and implementations are its home turf, docs/vision/27-strengths-bench.md §6); a predicted tie with fathom on the freshness task, since its gopls backend re-analyzes the file on disk on every call — no precomputed artifact to go stale.
serena.instructions_text:
## serena code navigation

Serena's own MCP tools are this repository's way to answer where a
symbol is defined, who calls it, and what breaks if it changes —
`find_symbol`, `find_referencing_symbols`, and
`find_implementations`, gopls-backed for Go. Read files to *edit*
them, not to discover them.

Reach for these first where they apply (who calls it, what breaks); elsewhere the nearest symbol lookup is still worth trying before grep.

Opening moves by task shape (first 1-2 calls, then edit):
- obligations: find_symbol to locate the governing file, then grep it for the rule
- claim_provenance: find_declaration for the symbol's site, then grep ADR.md for the citation
- concern_search: find_symbol by name pattern, then grep the doc comment text
- contradiction: find_symbol by name pattern, then grep both documents directly
- freshness: find_referencing_symbols, a live gopls query, then grep to confirm
- staleness: find_declaration, a live gopls query, then grep the cited file
- verify: find_symbol for the symbol's presence, then grep the plan/gate text directly
- blast_radius: find_referencing_symbols -> find_implementations, chained references

gopls.prediction: go_symbol_references/go_references answer code structure, not documented governance rules, so it is predicted to tie the grep arm (not fathom) on every obligations/verify/staleness lookup; a plausible tie with fathom on the 2-hop caller lookup (go_symbol_references chained twice) — single-language references is its home turf; a predicted tie with fathom on the freshness task, since it re-analyzes the file on disk on every call — no precomputed artifact to go stale. No find_implementations-equivalent is in its tool list here, so the interface-implementers lookup is predicted weaker than serena's, closer to a textual match.
gopls.instructions_text:
## gopls code navigation

gopls's own MCP tools are this repository's way to answer where a
symbol is defined, who calls it, and what breaks if it changes —
`go_search`, `go_symbol_references`, and `go_references`, backed by
a real type-checker. Read files to *edit* them, not to discover
them.

Reach for these first where they apply (who calls it, what breaks); elsewhere the nearest workspace query is still worth trying before grep.

Opening moves by task shape (first 1-2 calls, then edit):
- obligations: go_search for the symbol's neighbourhood, then grep the nearest CLAUDE.md / ADR.md
- claim_provenance: go_file_metadata for the file's own record, then grep ADR.md for the citation
- concern_search: go_search for a pattern over the workspace, then grep the doc comment text
- contradiction: go_search for a pattern over the workspace, then grep both documents directly
- freshness: go_symbol_references, a live on-disk query, then grep to confirm
- staleness: go_file_metadata, a live on-disk query, then grep the cited file
- verify: go_diagnostics for the file's own state, then grep the plan/gate text directly
- blast_radius: go_symbol_references -> go_references, chained references
